title: Three Replication Targets
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21 presents a city descending from heaven, radiant, with a jasper wall, twelve pearl gates, twelve gemstone foundations, and a street of transparent gold, lit without sun or moon.
engineering: Engineering view: the three targets are three separate engineering briefs, not one build. Target A is a navigable digital reconstruction of real Jerusalem geography and buildings. Target B is an illuminated transformation of Jerusalem, digital or as a physical installation. Target C is the visionary cube city of Revelation 21, treated as a design brief whose full-scale physical reproduction is not established.
body:
Target A uses real public tools and data: geographic information systems, satellite imagery, photogrammetry, laser scanning, and 3D engines such as Blender and Unreal Engine, with historical maps digitized period by period.

Targets B and C use established lighting practice at installation scale: addressable LED arrays, DMX and DALI control, and photometric verification. City-wide self-illumination without an energy source is not established and is never claimed here.

title: Cube Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city lies four-square, its length equal to its width and height, measured at 12,000 stadia, with a wall measured at 144 cubits.
engineering: Engineering view: the cube is a geometric specification, not a structural claim. A full-scale cube of that size cannot be built with known structural practice, so the cube record works at three scales: a full-scale mathematical model, an overview model, and a physical mock-up.
body:
Public geometry practice gives the cube its working tools: parametric modeling, Building Information Modeling, and CityGML city models, all of which can hold a 12,000-stadia cube as pure geometry.

The companion cube-city database carries the full measurement treatment, including stadion and cubit alternatives and the illustrative 2,220 km conversion.

title: Wall Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the wall is of jasper, great and high, measured at 144 cubits, with twelve gates set into it.
engineering: Engineering view: jasper-clad and jasper-inspired walls are achievable at installation and building scale using real stone, stone veneer, and engineered composites. A single continuous wall at the full visionary scale is not established.
body:
Real jasper is a microcrystalline quartz, opaque, commonly red, brown, or green, with a hardness near 7 on the Mohs scale; real stone suppliers and masonry practice cover cutting, coursing, jointing, and weatherproofing.

Wall prototypes in this suite use stone panels, veneer systems, and jasper-inspired composites, each with stated limits, rather than claiming a monolithic jasper wall.

title: Gates Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): twelve gates, three on each side, east, north, south, and west, each gate a single pearl, with the names of the twelve tribes inscribed.
engineering: Engineering view: a gate made from one single pearl at monumental scale is not a practical material, and this is stated plainly. The buildable interpretation is engineered nacre-inspired panels, pearlescent coatings, and panel assemblies, which require further research at gate scale.
body:
Real nacre is layered aragonite platelets in organic matrix, giving pearl its iridescence; real pearlescent coatings use mica-based pigments and interference films, both established at panel scale.

Gate assemblies use real structural practice: steel or timber frames, panel substrates, joints, and inspection access, with lighting designed so the gate reads as luminous without claiming supernatural radiance.

title: Foundations Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the twelve foundations of the wall are adorned with precious stones, named in order: jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprase, jacinth, and amethyst.
engineering: Engineering view: ancient stone names do not map one-to-one onto modern minerals, so every identification in this suite is an alternative, never a settled match. Real gemstone optics — refractive index, dispersion, absorption, color — are measurable and are carried in the gemstone-optics pair.
body:
Real public gemstone data covers the named families: sapphire as corundum with refractive index near 1.76, emerald as beryl near 1.57, topaz near 1.62, and amethyst as quartz near 1.54, each with documented color ranges.

Foundation courses at installation scale use cut stone, glass, and engineered composites with spectral data attached, so appearance claims stay tied to measurements.

title: Street Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the street of the city is pure gold, transparent as glass.
engineering: Engineering view: transparent gold is not a single known material. The buildable interpretation splits into two honest parts: a digital shader appearance for the digital city, and a physical recipe of laminated optical glass, metallic thin films, and dichroic coatings with explicit limits, never claimed identical to the text.
body:
Real physical options include laminated low-iron glass, gold-tinted metallic thin films, dichroic coatings, and transparent conductive films, each with measured transmission, reflection, and haze.

Street prototypes are walkable panels with stated slip resistance, load rating, and cleaning regimes, demonstrated at mock-up scale.

title: Radiance Summary
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God illuminates it, and there is no night there.
engineering: Engineering view: radiance is modeled, not reproduced. Digital radiance uses global illumination, emissive surfaces, and exposure control. Physical radiance uses powered lighting, and continuous no-night lighting at city scale is a research problem in energy, thermal management, and glare safety, not an established capability.
body:
Real lighting practice covers the pieces: LED and MicroLED arrays, fiber-optic distribution, addressable controllers, photometric testing, and glare analysis with published limits.

No-night mode in this suite is a simulation condition for the digital city and a scheduled lighting mode for installations, never a claim that a physical city needs no darkness.

engineering: Engineering view: the digital mode is demonstrated. Real-time engines, procedural city generation, level-of-detail systems, and volumetric rendering can present a navigable cube city, its gates, foundations, and street, at overview and district scales.
body:
Public digital tools include Blender, Unreal Engine, Unity, QGIS, and CityGML/CityJSON pipelines, with photogrammetry and point-cloud reconstruction feeding real Jerusalem geometry for target A.

Digital demos in this suite compute real geometry from stated parameters, so a visitor can check a dimension rather than take it on trust.

title: Physical Mode
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city is also described as a real place with walls, gates, and a street, which the physical mode honors by building touchable pieces at honest scales.
engineering: Engineering view: the physical mode is achievable at installation and mock-up scale: pavilions, gate prototypes, street panels, wall sections, and foundation courses, each commissioned with tests. Full-scale physical reproduction of the visionary city is not established.
body:
Real construction practice covers the pieces: masonry and stone panel systems, CNC cutting, robotic stone work, structural analysis, electrical safety, fire and emergency planning, and accessibility.

Every physical prototype in this suite carries a commissioning checklist with computed pass and fail results, so a claim of passing is always checkable.

title: Text-Faithful Versus Engineering Targets
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the text-faithful target keeps every described feature exactly as described — cube, jasper wall, pearl gates, gemstone foundations, transparent-gold street, radiance with no night — as the design brief.
engineering: Engineering view: the engineering target translates each feature into something measurable, with substitutions stated: nacre-inspired panels for single-pearl gates, shader plus laminate for transparent gold, powered lighting for radiance. The two targets are kept distinct on every record so a substitution is never mistaken for the original description.
body:
Public method for the split includes requirements databases, constraint records, uncertainty flags, and versioned interpretations, all standard systems-engineering practice.

Every record in this suite carries both views, so a reader can always see where the text ends and the engineering begins.

title: Scale-Aware Architecture
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the measuring angel measures city, gates, and wall together, which scale-aware architecture echoes by holding one specification across all scales.
engineering: Engineering view: scale-aware architecture is demonstrated practice. One parametric specification drives a full-scale mathematical model, an overview model for navigation, and a physical mock-up, with a scale manager stating which questions each scale can and cannot answer.
body:
Public scale practice includes parametric modeling, Building Information Modeling, digital twins with sensor feedback, and model-versus-physical scaling rules used in architecture and engineering.

A mock-up answers questions about joints, finishes, and light; it never answers questions about full-scale structure, and the scale manager says so.

title: Shared-Specification Principle

engineering: Engineering view: the shared-specification principle is demonstrated practice from parametric modeling and digital twins. One change to the specification updates geometry, materials, lighting, drawings, and tests together, so no view can silently drift from the others.
body:
Public tools for the principle include parametric Building Information Modeling, versioned requirements databases, and reproducible build pipelines with audit trails.

The demo counts the artifacts one change updates, so the principle is shown as arithmetic, not asserted as magic.
